candidate_sources.title: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides (anthracnose) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides causes anthracnose on banana with black and sunken lesions containing spore masses. Economic impact of 30-40% losses in commercial value. Control includes postharvest practices, sanitation, and both chemical and physical methods.

candidate_sources.title: Postharvest Rots of Banana
candidate_sources.snippet: Anthracnose appears as peel blemishes with black or brown, sunken spots of various sizes bearing masses of salmon-colored acervuli. Initial infection occurs during fruit development but remains latent until ripeness, with symptoms frequently becoming apparent during storage. Management includes prevention of infection and slowing symptom development.

candidate_sources.title: Colletotrichum musae (tip rot of banana)
candidate_sources.snippet: Colletotrichum musae is the fungus responsible for pre- and post-harvest banana anthracnose. Infection involves rapid spore germination and appressorium formation under favorable conditions: high relative humidity, temperatures 25-30°C, and neutral pH. Management focuses on preventing infection and slowing symptom development.

candidate_sources.title: First Report of Banana Anthracnose Caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides in Ecuador | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: First report of banana anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides in Ecuador. Symptoms characterized by sunken, circular lesions with dark-brown necrotic spots progressing to whitish mycelia and orange-colored conidial structures.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top virus (bunchy top of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: The Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV) is one of the most destructive plant pathogens affecting Musa species. It is a single-stranded DNA virus belonging to the genus Babuvirus and the family Nanoviridae. The pathogen is transmitted through vegetative planting material and by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa) in a circulative, non-propagative manner. Infected plants show bunchy top appearance with short, narrow, upright leaves; dark green streaks in leaf veins; and severe stunting.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Bunchy Top Virus
candidate_sources.snippet: Symptoms include progressive shortening and narrowing of new leaves creating a bunchy top appearance, dark green streaks in leaf midrib and petiole (Morse code streaking pattern), and severe stunting or dwarfing. Early infection results in plants that fail to produce fruit or produce small, misshapen fruit. The virus affects the phloem tissue causing cytopathological effects.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet: Bunchy top disease - What causes bunchy top?
candidate_sources.snippet: Bunchy top disease is caused by the Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV), a single-stranded DNA virus. The most distinctive symptom is the bunchy top appearance where new leaves are progressively shorter, narrower, and more upright, creating crowded appearance at the plant apex. The disease is transmitted by banana aphids and through infected planting material.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Bunchy Top: Detailed Signs and Symptoms
candidate_sources.snippet: The initial symptoms of banana bunchy top virus consist of dark green streaks in the veins of lower portions of the leaf midrib and the leaf stem. The streaks consist of dot-dash patterns, the so-called 'Morse code', the most diagnostic symptom of bunchy top. Infected plants display stunting and cessation of fruiting.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Bunchy Top Disease in Rwanda: Identifying Disease Presence and Potential Areas at Risk
candidate_sources.snippet: Banana bunchy top disease (BBTD), caused by banana bunchy top virus (BBTV, genus Babuvirus), is the most economically important viral disease of banana. Infection results in severe stunting and reduction in fruit production by 90-100% within two seasons.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot: Verticillium theobromae
candidate_sources.snippet: Cigar end rot of banana caused by fungus Verticillium theobromae. Characterized by dry gray to black rot at fruit tip with grayish fungal growth. Infection occurs at flowering stage during rainy season, spreading from flower to fruit tip.

candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive information on cigar end rot of banana. Covers symptoms characterized by dry rot at fruit tip resembling burnt cigar ash, pathogen information, disease development in warm moist conditions, and integrated management strategies including cultural practices and chemical controls.

candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed research on cigar end rot of banana caused by Musicillium theobromae and its control strategies in Egypt. Published in Archives of Phytopathology and Plant Protection, Vol 53, No 3-4.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana leaf spot | Improving the understanding of banana
candidate_sources.snippet: Cordana leaf spot is caused by two Neocordana fungi: Neocordana musae and Neocordana johnstonii. Symptoms include yellow or pale brown, oval- or eye-shaped spots appearing near leaf margins of lower leaves with clear concentric zonation. Spots may reach 10 cm and are diamond-shaped, pale brown with yellow border. Dispersal occurs via wet windy weather, and disease has generally little impact on production.
